newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends week slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends week slightly lower.

text.p: Morocco's bourse ended the week on Friday 0.09 lower, pulled down mainly by the banking sector, including blue-chip firms such as BCM and BMCE banks, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 665.53 points, down from 666.13 points on Wednesday.
The stock exchange was closed on Thursday for a public holiday.
"The bourse index slight drop is a simple correction. The market is expected to return soon to its upward trend," a bourse official said.
The index is showing a good performance as it rose 48.84 percent from 447.13 points in December 31, 1996, the official said.
Total traded volume jumped to 140.3 million dirhams from 98.9 million dirhams on Wednesday, he said.
But only a small amount of 23.9 million dirhams was exchanged on the official market, including 1.23 million dirhams of privatisation bonds, he added.
Launched in the second quarter of 1996, the second tranche of privatisation bonds dubbed "BDP 2" fell five dirhams to 1,255 dirhams.
With a capitalisation of 12 billion dirhamsn or the market's second largest firm, Banque Commerciale du Maroc, lost six dirhams to close at 909 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, a very liquid stock, also dropped by six dirhams to close at 580 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine pour le Developpement Economique, which expected to be privatised by end of this year, fell three dirhams to 225 dirhams.
Credit du Maroc, one of seven active banks on the bourse, closed at 455 dirhams, down five dirhams over the previous trading session.
Wafabank dipped four dirhams to close at 866 .
Morocco's largest private conglomerate, ONA Group ended the week at 830 dirhams from 832 dirhams.
Consumer credit firm Maroc Leasing, was down seven dirhams to 405 dirhams.
